title.narrative: Strengthened communications and constituents' capacity to analyse labour market indicators for better employment policies and services

description.narrative:
In 2025, the global context remained shaped by geopolitical instability and persistent inflation, generating uncertainty in trade, investment, and financial markets. In Brazil, domestic political dynamics also influenced policymaking, as the federal government faced challenges advancing its legislative agenda in a Congress with strong opposition.
Despite this environment, Brazilâ€™s economy showed resilience, with sustained growth and a strong labour market. Employment reached around 103 million people, while unemployment fell to approximately 5.2%, one of the lowest levels on record, reflecting continued job creation and labour market absorption.
However, structural challenges remained significant. Informality affected about 38% of workers, limiting access to labour rights and social protection. Although average earnings were around R$3,500 per month, disparities across sectors, regions, and demographic groups persisted, alongside concerns about job quality and access for young people.
These issues highlight the importance of promoting Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW). In response, the ILO Office for Brazil will support efforts in 2026â€“2027 to strengthen labour market data systems, enhance evidence-based policymaking, and improve the use of tools such as the SmartLab Observatory. Combined with stronger communication and outreach, these actions aim to support better decision-making, reinforce institutional coordination, and promote more inclusive labour market outcomes.
